title: Create a SHA-256 manifest for a local folder
goal: Record relative paths, file sizes and SHA-256 digests so a later copy can be compared with the original.
intro: Walk a trusted local folder in deterministic path order and hash each regular file in small chunks. Symlink files and directories are reported and skipped. File size and modification time are checked before and after reading, while file and byte limits bound the workload. The output is a JSON integrity inventory.
requirements: Python 3.10 or later; standard library only.
A trusted, stable local folder that is not a symlink.
Up to 10,000 files, 64 MiB per file and 256 MiB total; skipped links are bounded too.
limits: An integrity inventory is not a backup, signature or proof of authenticity. It does not restore files.
Symlinks are skipped; permissions, empty directories and extended attributes are not recorded.
The stable-folder assumption matters. This is not a locked filesystem snapshot or protection against an adversary changing paths while they are read.
steps: Choose a folder and stop changes while taking the inventory.
Write manifest.json outside the scanned folder so it is not included in a future inventory.
Repeat for a later copy and compare relative paths, byte sizes and SHA-256 values.
checks: Compare the digest of a known small file and an empty file.
Confirm deterministic ordering, nested relative paths and skipped symlinks.
Missing folders and count or byte-limit violations must return a nonzero exit status.
tested_scope: Executed locally with deterministic fixtures and CLI checks on Python 3.12.14. The three scripts pass 22 tests covering valid output, invalid input and size limits. No network or provider call was made.
